items.claim: The superscription row stands: every quoted run re-collates at byte tier against MT 1:1, the once-book-wide digit names the right object, and the frame seam is byte-clean.
items.evidence: Re-collated independently: the full-verse quote, the construct run שִׁ֥יר הַשִּׁירִ֖ים, and the relative clause אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִשְׁלֹמֹֽה all reach BYTE tier at oshb:Song.1.1. The digit is object-correct: the two-word run אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִשְׁלֹמֹֽה occurs in exactly 1 verse, and the relative-particle role likewise in 1 verse (MT 1:1). The frame seam is byte-clean: MT 1:2 carries no header form and no Shelomo token, so no device straddles Song.1.1|Song.1.2, and the parashah inventory (1 PE + 19 SAMEKH, single-witness, tier-3) places no seg at MT 1:1 - the row discloses that absence without treating it as evidence, which is correct. One folded nit, not fatal: the device-note universal that the book's relative particle is elsewhere the she-prefix carries no adjacent digit-bearing sweep and does not role-split the only other verse whose bytes contain the string (skeleton sweep: 2 verses; MT 6:9 וַֽיְאַשְּׁר֔וּהָ, a call-blessed verb) - a contained-substring homograph of the kerem-in-karmel class.
tier_citations: oshb:Song.6.9 (skeleton sweep: 2 verses bear the string; 1 verse bears the particle role)
parashah inventory (tier-3, single-witness; no seg at MT 1:1)

items.claim: The row files its dod signal under the beloved address vocabulary when the span's only dod-family bytes are the DEFECTIVE 'your loves' object, and three further attributions - verse position, marker location, cross-verse constancy - are imprecise against the bytes.
items.evidence: Both quoted runs do reach BYTE tier at their cited refs. The blend is at the object level: the span's only dod-family bytes are דֹּדֶ֖יךָ (oshb:Song.1.2, byte) and דֹדֶ֨יךָ֙ (oshb:Song.1.4, byte), both consonantally the vav-less spelling - the DEFECTIVE 'your loves' object (sweep: 4 verses - MT 1:2, MT 1:4, MT 4:10, MT 7:13 [= WEB 7:12]) - and neither MT 1:2 nor MT 1:4 appears in the dodi-exact list (24 verses) or the dod-family list (28 verses). Filing this span under the dodi address vocabulary is the five-object blend the hazard catalog names, and it bites here because the row's voice attribution leans on that key. Second, oshb:Song.1.4 is called the unit's second verse; in the span Song.1.2-Song.1.4 it is the third. Third, the 2ms marking of מָשְׁכֵ֖נִי אַחֲרֶ֣יךָ (oshb:Song.1.4, byte) sits on אַחֲרֶ֣יךָ (final kaf with qamats), not on the imperative's suffix, which is 1cs; 'imperative-plus-suffix address' mis-locates the marker. Fourth, the claim that the 2ms addressee holds across all three verses quotes nothing from MT 1:3, where the byte-available markers actually are (שְׁמָנֶ֣יךָ, שְׁמֶ֑ךָ, אֲהֵבֽוּךָ, all byte at oshb:Song.1.3), and it leaves undisclosed the one form in MT 1:4 that is genuinely contested - בָּ֔ךְ (byte), a kaf that is 2fs in form and 2ms only on a pausal reading, unsettleable with no morphology layer staged.
tier_citations: sweep: 24 verses (dodi-exact) / 28 verses (dod-family) - neither list contains MT 1:2 or MT 1:4

items.claim: The row's closing-seam driver is byte-false in position and is voice-identity rather than voice-shift evidence, and no Hebrew at all is quoted from MT 1:6.
items.evidence: The opening arm holds: בְּנ֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם reaches BYTE tier at oshb:Song.1.5 and is a true vocative (address object: 6 verses; the same skeleton also returns the MT 3:10 from-phrase, correctly not counted here). The closing arm does not. The row names the she-ahavah-nafshi formula as opening Song.1.7: MT 1:7 opens הַגִּ֣ידָה לִּ֗י (byte; sweep: 1 verse book-wide for that opener), and שֶׁ֤אָהֲבָה֙ נַפְשִׁ֔י (byte) stands as the verse's third and fourth tokens - not its opener. More substantively, that formula is HER formula (sweep: 5 verses - MT 1:7, 3:1, 3:2, 3:3, 3:4) and MT 1:5-1:6 is also her voice, so it cannot carry a speaker change at MT 1:6|1:7; it marks voice identity, not voice shift. The byte marker that does sit at the seam is an ADDRESSEE flip the row never quotes: the plural אַל תִּרְא֨וּנִי֙ (oshb:Song.1.6, byte) addressing the daughters, against the singular 2ms תִרְעֶ֔ה with חֲבֵרֶֽיךָ (oshb:Song.1.7, byte) addressing the man. With no Hebrew quoted from MT 1:6, the claim that no addressee change interrupts the run through the end of that verse rests on the English rendering alone.

items.claim: The single-verse holding is byte-sound, but the formula's byte position is misstated and the 2ms gender claim is asserted on a morphologically ambiguous form whose in-verse disambiguator is never quoted.
items.evidence: Both quotes reach BYTE tier at oshb:Song.1.7 and the device-note digit is object-correct (she-ahavah-nafshi formula, sweep: 5 verses - MT 1:7, 3:1, 3:2, 3:3, 3:4). Two defects. (1) שֶׁ֤אָהֲבָה֙ נַפְשִׁ֔י does not open MT 1:7; the verse opens הַגִּ֣ידָה לִּ֗י (byte). (2) תִרְעֶ֔ה is a prefix-conjugation form ambiguous between 2ms and 3fs, and NO morphology layer is staged; the 2ms reading is fixed only by the unambiguous 2ms token later in the same verse, חֲבֵרֶֽיךָ (byte), alongside the parallel תַּרְבִּ֣יץ (byte) - the row quotes neither, so as written the gender claim is asserted where it should be held on the quoted bytes. The forward arm (that MT 1:8 flips every verb and suffix to 2fs) is byte-true but carries no adjacent digit and no quoted form: MT 1:8 shows 6 such markers - תֵדְעִי֙, לָ֔ךְ, צְֽאִי, לָ֔ךְ, וּרְעִי֙, גְּדִיֹּתַ֔יִךְ (all byte at oshb:Song.1.8).

items.claim: The row argues a four-verse single-addressee unit while leaving the one tier-1 address anchor inside its own span uncited and carrying three of its four verses on the English rendering alone.
items.evidence: The seam arm holds at byte tier: תֵדְעִי֙, צְֽאִי and וּרְעִי֙ all collate byte at oshb:Song.1.8. But רַעְיָתִֽי stands in oshb:Song.1.9 (byte) - his word for her, the attested tier-1 address anchor (sweep: 9 verses - MT 1:9, 1:15, 2:2, 2:10, 2:13, 4:1, 4:7, 5:2, 6:4) - inside this row's own span and never cited, alongside the 2fs object suffix on דִּמִּיתִ֖יךְ (byte). For MT 1:9-1:11 the row quotes no Hebrew whatever: English glosses stand in for לְחָיַ֨יִךְ֙ and צַוָּארֵ֖ךְ (oshb:Song.1.10, byte) and נַעֲשֶׂה לָּ֔ךְ (oshb:Song.1.11, byte), so three of the four verses of the continuity claim are translation-carried. Two byte-level slips: תֵדְעִי֙ is glossed as a negated form, but the negation lies in the unquoted אִם לֹ֤א (byte), and MT 1:8 opens with those two tokens, not with the 2fs form the row says opens the unit. Credit where due, and audited against the modern editorial voice apparatus: the row declines to follow the apparatus site at WEB 1:11 and grounds the refusal on the absence of a gender-marked form - that arm audits clean.
tier_citations: WEB voice apparatus (tier-4, audit only - not leaned on by the row)

items.claim: A voice-shift seam is asserted with no gender-marked form quoted on either side of it, and two of the book's twelve paseq verses sit inside this three-verse span undisclosed.
items.evidence: The recurrence itself is real and stronger than the row states: דּוֹדִי֙ לִ֔י reaches BYTE tier at oshb:Song.1.13 and the identical string reaches BYTE tier at oshb:Song.1.14 - a byte-tier, not skeleton-tier, recurrence. Three defects. (1) The seam this row asserts is MT 1:11|1:12, described as a shift out of 2fs address into her first-person voice, yet no Hebrew is quoted at that seam from either side: the 2fs form in MT 1:11 is נַעֲשֶׂה לָּ֔ךְ (byte) and MT 1:12's only first-person marker is נִרְדִּ֖י (byte), a 1cs possessive that is gender-unmarked, the rest of the verse being third-person around שֶׁ֤הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ (byte, the melek lexeme - sweep: 5 verses). The owner voice policy's byte arm wants the gender-marked form AT the seam; the two byte quotes offered sit one and two verses past it, so the row's own tier-2 concession for MT 1:12 is carrying the seam. (2) Span-relevant disclosure symmetry is incomplete: the SAMEKH at MT 1:14 is disclosed, but the paseq segs at MT 1:13 AND MT 1:14 - 2 of the book's 12 paseq verses, both inside this 3-verse span (seg layer, single-witness, count-only) - are not. (3) The 24-verse digit names the right object (dodi-exact) but sits immediately beside a twice-quoted TWO-word run whose own count is 4 verses (MT 1:13, MT 1:14, MT 2:16, MT 6:3, skeleton tier), inviting exactly the digit-object slippage the hazard catalog warns about.
tier_citations: paseq inventory MT 1:13 + MT 1:14 (seg layer, single-witness, count-only)
sweep: 4 verses (the two-word run, skeleton tier)

items.claim: The exchange's opening is the cluster's best byte evidence, but its closing seam at MT 2:3|2:4 carries no byte evidence, no forward neighbour ref, and is crossed by an unbroken single-speaker configuration the row never discloses.
items.evidence: All four quotes reach BYTE tier at their refs, and הִנָּ֤ךְ (oshb:Song.1.15, byte - 2fs) against הִנְּךָ֨ (oshb:Song.1.16, byte - 2ms) is precisely the gender-marked pair the voice policy asks for; רַעְיָתִ֔י/דוֹדִי֙ and כֵּ֥ן רַעְיָתִ֖י/כֵּ֥ן דּוֹדִ֖י are attested, object-correct address anchors. The defect is the closing seam. Nothing in the row argues MT 2:3|2:4 and no forward neighbour ref appears (the only neighbour cited is backward), while the bytes run straight across the cut: MT 2:3's חִמַּ֣דְתִּי, וְיָשַׁ֔בְתִּי, לְחִכִּֽי (byte, 1cs) continue into MT 2:4's הֱבִיאַ֨נִי֙ and עָלַ֖י with 3ms וְדִגְל֥וֹ (byte) - same speaker configuration, no vocative, no address-vocabulary token and no gender-marked addressee change at the cut. Cross-seam continuity of that kind argues continuity against the row unless disclosed, and it is not. Secondary: the 1cp chain that keeps MT 1:17 inside her turn - עַרְשֵׂ֖נוּ (oshb:Song.1.16, byte) into בָּתֵּ֨ינוּ֙ and רַהִיטֵ֖נוּ (oshb:Song.1.17, byte) - is argued from the English with no Hebrew quoted, and the token leaned on is the qere in the span's one K/Q verse (inventory: 4 K/Q notes book-wide, MT 1:17 among them), which the row simultaneously declares it makes no K/Q claim about. MT 2:1 (אֲנִי֙ חֲבַצֶּ֣לֶת, byte, gender-unmarked) is left unattributed inside a unit whose entire warrant is attributed alternation.
tier_citations: K/Q inventory MT 1:17 (4 notes book-wide, single-witness)
